pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

Applying porcelain slip onto a moon jar.  I love this approach because stoneware is strong and much easier to work with, especially when throwing large forms. Adding porcelain slip later gives you that softness and elegance on the surface. Best of both worlds. ✅ A few tips: Apply the slip at leather hard so both clays shrink evenly and bond well. If you wait too long after trimming, and you pour at the bone dry stage.. you might find your moon jar disintegrating right in front of you. Speaking from experience 😅 Keep a close eye on drying. The added moisture from the slip can soften the stoneware walls and cause the jar to squat or sag if you are not careful. Good slip prep is key. Right consistency, smooth, and deflocculated if needed. Here the slip was thick as I was going for a rougher finish 😊 different from what I'd normally do. . . . . . #porcelain #ceramics #ceramiccoating #foryoupage #viral

Throwing a Donut on the Wheel Center your clay and compress it into a wide, flat puck. Poke through the center down to the wheel head and slowly stretch it open to create the donut hole. Split the ring 50/50—leave a base slightly thicker than your future walls. Pull up the inner wall first, then the outer wall. Join the walls together. It doesn’t matter which one overlaps—adjust based on how the clay moves. Before joining, I thin out the edges to avoid a step at the seam. Important! Remove any slip and excess water from the seam—otherwise, it will crack during drying or firing. Once the walls are joined, the trapped air inside acts as a support structure, allowing you to refine the shape and compress the seam. Trim the excess clay inside and out, and your donut is ready! Follow me for more wheel-throwing tips! … … #ceramics #potteryvideos #pottery #fyp #usa
